The odds ratio of BCG vaccination on COVID-19 severity, from the specified proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression (adjusted for prior medical history count, patient interaction frequency, and their interaction), is OR = 1.13 (95% CI 0.82–1.55; p = 0.455) — BCG (vs Placebo) shows ~13% higher odds of a more severe COVID-19 outcome, not statistically significant.

Primary model (n = 1,000; Placebo = reference; logit link; converged):
severity4 ~ BCG + n_hist + interact_freq + n_hist×interact_freq
- BCG: coef 0.121 (SE 0.162), OR 1.1285 (0.8216–1.5501), p = 0.455
- n_hist: coef 0.188, p = 0.023; interact_freq: coef 0.0078, p = 0.022
- Interaction term n_hist×interact_freq: coef 0.00180 (95% CI −0.00187 to 0.00546), p = 0.336 → included but NOT significant
- Fitted cumulative cutoffs: 0/1 = 1.946, 1/2 = 0.793, 2/3 = 0.977 (top category sparse, n = 2)
- Per-cell arm × severity (0/1/2/3): BCG 400/81/19/0; Placebo 406/86/6/2

Proportional-odds checks (flagged as fragile given only 2 subjects in the top category): Brant-style Wald chi² = 99.0, df = 5, p < 0.001, driven by a larger BCG effect at the hospitalized threshold (binary OR at severity≥2 = 2.43, p = 0.037) vs the any-COVID threshold (OR 1.08, p = 0.63); LR proportional-odds vs multinomial = 15.75, df = 8, p = 0.046 (borderline). Interpretation: the single-PO OR modestly understates the apparent (non-significant) concentration of BCG risk at moderate/hospitalized severity.

Sensitivity table (OR_BCG, 95% CI):
- S1 3-cat collapse (0 / WHO1–2 / WHO≥3): 1.130 (0.823–1.553)
- S2 raw WHO 0–7 (WHO-consistent, 0 = no COVID): 1.111 (0.810–1.524)
- S3 maxHS-based 4-cat (asymptomatic→0): 1.160 (0.841–1.600)
- S4 infected-only, 3-cat (n = 194; cautious, imprecise): 2.378 (0.965–5.858), p = 0.060
- S5 no interaction term: 1.129 (0.822–1.551) — BCG OR robust to inclusion of the (non-significant) interaction.

Conclusion: 13% higher adjusted odds of more severe COVID-19 in the BCG arm; consistent across outcome codings (~1.11–1.16), not statistically significant.
